limitations: One sequence, one perturbation, 3 invocation(s) per backend. Repetitions measure timing on the same frames, not independent recovery trials. Bootstrap intervals do not establish statistical confidence for this demo.
All invocations, including the first, contribute to timing. There is no separate warm-up or cold-process guarantee; lazy compilation and process-wide caches affect latency.
Optimizer convergence and CPU/GPU parity do not establish calibration accuracy. Dataset reference is not independent metrology; covariance/observability remain unknown.
Only the supplied frozen provider frames are eligible; uniform selection is by position within that provider. Learned depth and frame synchronization can bias the fit.
Provider training/evaluation overlap: possible. official non-online-refined checkpoint selected; repository does not publish enough training IDs to exclude drive overlap
training/evaluation drive overlap cannot be excluded
raw FeatDepth inverse-depth/disparity is retained for D2D histograms
metric depth conversion parameters are recorded but not applied
Three invocations per method on one workload with cyclic execution order. Shared host is not isolated; no speed guarantee or statistical confidence.
Pipeline phases include verification/loading, backend preparation, solve, and holdout/pool shutdown; exclude shared setup, serialization, and report rendering.
Both GPU modes use the same unchanged FP64 kernels; reference explicitly selects the single-frame API through a bound launcher wrapper.
First CPU includes compilation from an absent cache; first CUDA serial reference includes NVRTC preparation. Later invocations share compiled caches.

protocol.failure_policy: Retain every invocation, numerical mismatch, and nonconvergence.
protocol.initial_estimate_policy: Controlled demo initialization: dataset reference plus fixed local Euler offsets. Rotation deg xyz=(0.5, 0.0, 0.0); camera-frame translation m xyz=(0.5, 0.0, 0.0). This is not an independently measured prior.
protocol.split_policy: 25 numeric-ordered, uniformly selected provider positions; every fifth frame is holdout (20 fit / 5 holdout), fixed before optimization.
protocol.tuning_policy: Same solver settings for both backends; no holdout tuning.
